"""Starting architecture: the main campaign's default policy (conv encoder, width 64, depth 2, ReLU,
no normalisation), rewritten as a candidate file. A 3x3 conv body, a 1x1 conv placement head
(one logit per brick type and anchor cell), and DONE and value heads on mean+max pooled features."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The baseline's 4 seeds (0.068 ×3, 0.258 ×1) show that a run either reaches a high mode or stalls, so one 2-seed mean is weak evidence. Under the default recipe the run gets about 131k steps in only 32 updates of 4096 samples, which is very few policy improvements. Since only the recipe can change, the first round tests two budget levers and one credit-assignment lever. The first two cut PPO epochs to buy more samples, which gives about 2-3x the data and about 100+ updates; the default epoch count may be using up the budget for little gain. The third makes credit assignment longer-horizon, because the +1 exact-build bonus comes only at episode end, up to 41 steps away, and gamma 0.95 discounts it heavily.
analyses.2: All three round-1 recipes scored exactly 0.0684 on both seeds. The baseline's three failed seeds scored the same, and it sits at 35 of 512 dev designs. This identical score points to one stable low-success policy that training falls into, not to random spread. Training success also stays near 0.06. Only one of 4 baseline seeds escaped to 0.258. Changing the sample count, the epoch count or the reward horizon left the agent stuck. The likely bottleneck is the agent locking into a weak policy too early, so it stops trying alternatives. That makes exploration pressure (entropy) and update size (learning rate, PPO epochs) the next things to test. To beat the 0.116 baseline mean, a recipe has to escape on most seeds, and only a score clearly different from 0.0684 tells us anything. Each candidate changes one main factor so its result can be read clearly.
analyses.3: Five of the six recipes gave exactly 0.0684 on both seeds. That matches three of the four baseline seeds, so the 0.0684 is a stable mode the runs fall into, not noise. Only one baseline seed ever escaped it (0.258). Changing epochs, entropy or learning rate alone did not change the outcome. Eight epochs made things worse (0.045), so reusing data heavily hurts here. Long-horizon credit (gamma 0.99) has only been tested with 4 epochs and the default short rollouts. Untested directions: myopic credit (a low gamma, which the dense per-cell reward supports, with less variance), longer rollouts (fewer value-bootstrap cuts inside 41-step episodes), and large, low-noise batches with a gentle learning rate. Each proposal below changes how credit is assigned or how much the gradients vary, which is the most likely way to leave this mode.
analyses.4: Six trials of the 1-epoch recipe all landed exactly on 0.0684 on both seeds. That held whatever the entropy, learning rate, discount or rollout length, and 0.0684 is also the baseline's usual score. So 0.0684 is a stable weak policy. Recipes that took gentle steps (lr 3e-4) made too few updates and fell below it. The only run that escaped was a baseline seed (0.258) on the default 4-epoch recipe at lr 1e-3. The likely bottleneck is how many effective optimisation steps the policy gets, not how many samples it sees: the 1-epoch recipes took fewer gradient steps per sample and never got out. For this last round I keep 4 or 3 epochs and push harder on optimisation: more and smaller minibatches with a wider clip, a sharper policy (no entropy bonus, higher lr), and many small updates. Seed noise is large. A trial counts as evidence only if a seed clearly beats 0.0684.
